panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra stops the procurement debate at a working table and asks the nearby crew for the tasks that actually need protection; no posed six-person lineup.

PANEL 2 — Two compact job-site vignettes within one sequential panel: Zib indicates a clear maintenance bench and an actual replacement-part request; Jax holds his route slate and points out that collection paths must stay operational. Both speakers are identifiable.
PANEL 3 — At the same table, Mira keeps the physical sample vial separate from Glorp's custody form. Mira insists on testable evidence and Glorp on records without private diaries.

PANEL 4 — Kreeb stands by Jax's completed custody log and gives the last practical boundary: a coworker gathering must not become a participation survey. Astra can acknowledge from the frame edge without another balloon.

summary: At the admin-hub worktable, Astra asks the crew for concrete operating boundaries rather than speeches. Zib and Jax describe maintenance and routing, Mira and Glorp describe evidence and privacy, and Kreeb ends with the human consequence beside Jax's completed custody log.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax completes the bounded passive-collection route log at the local terminal while ordinary end-of-shift cleanup starts. A closed collection container remains beside the route slate.

PANEL 2 — Pixa checks that no emotional or personal fields entered the submission, then mentions Mira's gathering and the invitations she offered to organize. Keep this a Jax–Pixa exchange, not a crowd around the terminal.
PANEL 3 — Glorp comes to collect the custody sheet and asks Pixa whether she is actually attending or only maintaining the calendar. Jax can leave the frame with the completed route slate.
PANEL 4 — Pixa looks directly at Glorp and admits that she would like to attend herself. This is an unhurried character beat, not an electronic announcement.
PANEL 5 — Kreeb hears the conversation while bringing an access sign to the nearby collection rack and tells Pixa she is welcome. The physical rack remains clear of door and service access.
PANEL 6 — Pixa takes in the simple invitation. Hold her response and Kreeb's friendly reaction without displaying a full crew assembled to celebrate.

PANEL 7 — Quiet operational closing view: Zib's safely positioned collection bins and the one short instruction card—ACCESS FIRST / PASSIVE COLLECTION SECOND—remain at the rack. The pilot continues as ordinary work, not a new program ceremony.

summary: Seven small end-of-shift beats reconcile the bounded passive-collection job with Pixa's wish to be invited as a person, not only as a scheduler. Jax closes the accurate route log, Pixa speaks about Mira's gathering, Glorp asks her intention, Kreeb welcomes her, and Zib leaves a single usable access-first instruction on the collection rack.
